body.statement: Under assignment positivity, let \(N_j=(n_0,n_1,m_1,m_0)\), \(w_j=(1,1,2,2)\), and \(\varepsilon_j=\sqrt{\log(2/\beta_j)/(2N_j)}\). Uniformly over compatible primitives with \(d\ge\kappa\), with probability at least \(1-\beta\), \[K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}\subseteq[\inf K^{\star}-R,\sup K^{\star}+R]\cap[0,1],\qquad R=\frac{2}{\kappa}\sum_jw_j\varepsilon_j.\] In addition, \(\sup_P E_P[\{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-\operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}]=O(1/(\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}))\) for fixed marginal budgets. These claims use only the four marginal binomial laws and do not require their counts to be mutually independent.
body.justification: Coverage alone can be vacuous; the width theorem quantifies the statistical price of weak assay informativeness and four primitive intervals.
body.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019 establishes uniform asymptotic coverage for generic moment projections but not an exact finite-sample width modulus indexed by the Youden floor.
body.consumer: Validation-study designers can translate a desired benefit-interval precision into trial and gold-standard stratum sizes.
body.proof_tex:
We first derive a deterministic modulus.  Along any segment joining two compatible primitive tuples \(\eta=(q_0,q_1,u,v)\) and \(\eta'=(q'_0,q'_1,u',v')\), the linear compatibility inequalities and \(v-u\geq\kappa\) remain valid.  For
\[
 p_a=\frac{q_a-u}{v-u}
\]
direct differentiation gives
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial q_a}\right|=\frac1d,qquad
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial u}\right|=\frac{v-q_a}{d^2}=\frac{1-p_a}{d},qquad
 \left|\frac{\partial p_a}{\partial v}\right|=\frac{q_a-u}{d^2}=\frac{p_a}{d}.
\]
All three are at most \(1/\kappa\).  Combining segment integration with the root's unit margin Lipschitz bound yields, uniformly in \(\theta\),
\[
 |b(\eta,\theta)-b(\eta',\theta)|
 \leq\frac{|q_0-q'_0|+|q_1-q'_1|+2|u-u'|+2|v-v'|}{\kappa}.
\]
Since \(|u-u'|=|c-c'|\) and \(|v-v'|=|s-s'|\), this is the asserted weighting of the four primitive coordinates.

Next bound each Clopper--Pearson interval.  If \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,p)\) and \(Q_\gamma(X)=[L_X,U_X]\) is its two-sided interval, an interior upper endpoint satisfies the defining lower-tail equation \(\Pr_{U_X}(X'\leq X)=\gamma/2\).  When \(U_X>X/N\), the cited Hoeffding inequality gives
\[
 \frac\gamma2\leq\exp\{-2N(U_X-X/N)^2\},
\]
and hence
\[
 U_X-X/N\leq\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}}.
\]
The lower endpoint follows from the other tail; boundary endpoints \(0\) and \(1\) satisfy the corresponding one-sided claim directly.  Therefore
\[
 Q_\gamma(X)\subseteq
 \left[X/N-\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}},
       X/N+\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\gamma)}{2N}}\right]\cap[0,1].
\]

On the simultaneous primitive-coverage event from the exact-projection theorem, both a feasible projected coordinate and the truth lie in the same primitive interval.  Their coordinate differences are therefore at most \(2\varepsilon_j\).  The deterministic modulus gives, for every feasible projected tuple and every \(\theta\),
\[
 |b(\widetilde\eta,\theta)-b(\eta^{\star},\theta)|
 \leq R:=\frac2\kappa\sum_jw_j\varepsilon_j.
\]
The true tuple is itself feasible on this event, so exact projection gives the first inclusion.  Taking the infimum and supremum over projected tuples in the last display gives
\[
 K^{\star}\subseteq I_{\beta}
 \subseteq[\inf K^{\star}-R,\sup K^{\star}+R]\cap[0,1].
\]
The event has probability at least \(1-\beta\), and no independence among counts entered either this step or the union bound.

For the expectation claim, let \(\widehat p_j\) denote the four empirical proportions and define
\[
 R_{\mathrm{data}}=\frac1\kappa
 \sum_jw_j\bigl(|\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star}|+\varepsilon_j\bigr).
\]
The interval containment just proved shows, without conditioning on primitive coverage, that every coordinate in a primitive interval is within \(|\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star}|+\varepsilon_j\) of the truth.  The modulus therefore implies, taking the length of an empty projection to be zero,
\[
 \{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-
       \operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}
 \leq2R_{\mathrm{data}}.
\]
For a binomial empirical proportion,
\[
 E|\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star}|
 \leq\sqrt{E(\widehat p_j-p_j^{\star})^2}
 =\sqrt{\frac{p_j^{\star}(1-p_j^{\star})}{N_j}}
 \leq\frac1{2\sqrt{N_j}}.
\]
Consequently
\[
 \sup_P E_P\{\operatorname{length}(I_{\beta})-
       \operatorname{length}(K^{\star})\}_{+}
 \leq\frac2\kappa\sum_jw_j
 \left\{\frac1{2\sqrt{N_j}}+\varepsilon_j\right\}
 =O\!\left(\frac1{\kappa\sqrt{N_{\min}}}\right)
\]
when the four marginal budgets are fixed.  Every bound is uniform in the compatible primitive probabilities.
